label: D2 after a rare a2->S1 transition (repeat a2 choice), late in the episode
explanation: Fires only at D2 (zero on D1 and GO), and only when the agent chose a2 and landed in S1, i.e. a rare transition for a2 (in_action=2, in_state=1; 26484 of 26493 activations). It does not fire on a1 trials, common transitions, or rare a1->S2. It is also strongly gated by episode time: no activity before about trial 30, it ramps up over trials 30-49, and it saturates from about 50 on. Adding ep_trial>=45 raises precision from 0.49 to 0.82. Requiring that the a2 choice was not a switch from a1 (stay != 0) raises dev F1 to 0.915 (P 0.87, R 0.96, mass recall 0.99). All variables are observable at D2. The ep_trial term is not an input; the agent would have to track elapsed time implicitly. Weak activations are concentrated near the onset boundary (trials 40-49). Remaining false positives include some cases where S1 was the good state. I did not establish what modulates magnitude within the firing set.

issues: All the factual claims check out on dev. Every activation is at D2 (zero on D1 and GO). 26484 of 26493 activations have action=2 and in_state=1, and only 9 fire with action=1. The predicate without the time term scores P 0.487, R 1.00. Adding ep_trial>=45 gives P 0.82 and F1 0.889. The full predicate gives P 0.871, R 0.965, F1 0.915, mass recall 0.993. On test it gives P 0.853, R 0.964, F1 0.905, mass recall 0.992, matching the reported scores.

The time gating is real and monotonic. Within (D2, a2->S1, stay!=0), precision by ep_trial is: trials 0-29 0.00, 30-37 0.03, 38-41 0.12, 42-44 0.28, 45-47 0.62, 48-51 0.79, 52-59 0.88, 60-99 0.90. The onset therefore falls near trials 45-50 rather than 30; activity in trials 30-44 is tiny (mass recall 0.005 for 30-44).

The stay exclusion holds up. With stay==0 (switching from a1 to a2), precision is 0.06 with 0.2% of the mass. Note that 'stay != 0' also admits stay==-1, the window's first trial, where the previous choice is unknown; those score P 0.87, so 'repeat a2 choice' is slightly loose but not wrong.

The remaining false positives (about 13-15%) have mild structure, all pointing to the agent holding weaker confidence that S2 is good: when good==S1, precision is 0.65 (recall share 0.13). After a common-unrewarded previous trial, precision is 0.61. When the agent will switch on the next trial (next_stay==0, which is future and reward-dependent), precision is 0.27 (1.7% recall). None of these refinements improves test F1 meaningfully: excluding good==S1 after an established reversal gives test F1 0.898, excluding prev common-unrewarded gives 0.876, and adding next_stay!=0 gives 0.913 but uses a future variable. So this is a graded modulation, not a missing class.
The explanation says activity 'ramps up over trials 30-49'. Firing is negligible before about trial 42 and ramps mostly over trials 42-52, a minor imprecision.
